question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{y}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{y}{3}) \\ {10}^{x} & ={10}^{\operatorname{log}⁡(y/3)} \\ {10}^{x} & =\frac{y}{3} \\ y & =3\cdot {10}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=3\cdot {10}^{x}.$
